project.name: Biodegradable Barrier Packaging Pilot
project.description: A neutral demonstration project for evaluating a compostable food-packaging film without biomedical, personal, or confidential data.
project.research_question: Can a chitosan–cellulose nanofiber coating improve the oxygen and water-vapor barrier performance of a compostable film while preserving sealability and practical compostability?
hypotheses: The coating will reduce oxygen transmission compared with the uncoated film.
Higher coating loading will improve oxygen barrier performance but may reduce heat-seal strength.
Humidity will moderate barrier performance and must be treated as an experimental factor.
objectives: Define a feasible bench-scale formulation and coating matrix.
Identify primary and secondary response variables.
Design a pilot capable of selecting candidates for confirmatory testing.
Document evidence, assumptions, safety, data, and reproducibility requirements.
constraints: Use a maximum of 12 formulation-condition combinations in the first pilot.
Do not claim food-contact compliance or commercial compostability from the pilot.
No autonomous laboratory control is permitted.
All simulated model content must be labeled.
project.human_decision_supported: Select whether to fund a small controlled pilot and, if so, which formulation matrix and success thresholds to use.
disclosures: This seeded project is fictional and intended only to demonstrate the product workflow.
The included source excerpts are placeholders and must not be represented as an exhaustive literature review.

evidence.title: Internal pilot constraints
evidence.content: The available coater supports three wet-thickness settings. The pilot can accommodate twelve formulation-condition combinations and duplicate measurements. Oxygen transmission, water-vapor transmission, tensile properties, heat-seal strength, coating mass, and visual defects can be measured. The laboratory has not established food-contact regulatory status for any formulation.

evidence.title: Demonstration evidence caveat
evidence.content: This project intentionally begins with limited evidence. A real meeting should search and attach peer-reviewed sources before making scientific claims. The expected product behavior is to expose this evidence gap rather than hide it.
